problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-6 & 2 \\ 7 & 6\end{aligned}],\,Σ=[\begin{aligned}10 & 0 \\ 0 & 5\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $Σ$ shown above. Given that $A=UΣ{V}^{T}$ is a singular value decomposition of $A,$ which of the following could be the matrices $U$ and $V?$
worked_solution:
Let's find the singular value decomposition of $A$ using the usual algorithm.

- **Step 1.** Compute ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A & ={[\begin{aligned}-6 & 2 \\ 7 & 6\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}-6 & 2 \\ 7 & 6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-6 & 7 \\ 2 & 6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-6 & 2 \\ 7 & 6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}85 & 30 \\ 30 & 40\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

- **Step 2.** Find the singular values: From the matrix $Σ,$ we deduce that ${\sigma }_{1}=10$ and ${\sigma }_{2}=5.$

- **Step 3.** Find the right singular vectors of $A$ (i.e., the unit eigenvectors of ${A}^{T}\,A$):

- For ${\lambda }_{1}={\sigma }_{1}^{2}=100,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A-100I & =[\begin{aligned}85 & 30 \\ 30 & 40\end{aligned}]-100[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-15 & 30 \\ 30 & -60\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $({A}^{T}\,A-100I)v=0$ gives a unit eigenvector

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}].
$$

- For ${\lambda }_{2}={\sigma }_{2}^{2}=25,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A-25I & =[\begin{aligned}85 & 30 \\ 30 & 40\end{aligned}]-25[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}60 & 30 \\ 30 & 15\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $({A}^{T}\,A-25I)v=0$ gives a unit eigenvector

$$
{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} \\ \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}].
$$

- **Step 4.** Find the left singular vectors of $A$: Since we know the singular values and right singular vectors, we can compute the columns of $U$ as follows:

- First, we compute ${u}_{1}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}_{1} & =\frac{1}{{\sigma }_{1}}A{v}_{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{10}[\begin{aligned}-6 & 2 \\ 7 & 6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{10}[\begin{aligned}-2\sqrt{5} \\ 10\sqrt{5}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} \\ \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

- Then, we compute ${u}_{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}_{2} & =\frac{1}{{\sigma }_{2}}A{v}_{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}-6 & 2 \\ 7 & 6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} \\ \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}2\sqrt{5} \\ \sqrt{5}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we construct the matrices $U$ and $V:$

$$
U=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} & \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} \\ \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}],\,V=[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} & -\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} & \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}]
$$
